resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 supported. Package 6 (EWPS-4 to EWPS-6, EWGP-3/EWGP-4) is part of Aramco MGS Phase 3; Blackridge gives expected completion Q4 2028; SPA (official Aramco $25bn gas-expansion announcement, Jul 2024) states the program adds ~3.15 bscfd 'by 2028'; pipeline-journal (L&T completion) also cites 2028 target. Independent origins (research profile / official PR / trade journal). Flag: OGJ (Sinopec Packages 6+7 award) cites mechanical completion May 31, 2027 for the EPC contract, slightly earlier than the 2028 operations/completion date — 2028 in GEM is consistent with program completion, not a contradiction of the start value.

LengthKnown=185 km is NOT directly stated by any source found. Blackridge describes Package 6 as 'Lay 56-inch diameter pipelines (EWGP-3 and EWGP-4) from EWPS-4 to EWPS-6 (370 km)' — i.e. 370 km for the PAIR of parallel pipes. GEM splits this into two rows (this row is EWGP-3, the '3' pipe), so 185 km = 370/2 is a per-pipe derivation, not a quoted figure. Ref supports the 370 km/pair context; the 185 km per-pipe value should be treated as derived/inferred. OGJ (Sinopec Packages 6+7) gives 696 km for the two packages combined, consistent with ~370 km for Package 6. No source found stating 185 km explicitly.

StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia supported. The EWPS-4 to EWPS-6 line runs within Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province (Blackridge: 'Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia'; OGJ: Saudi Arabia). East-West pipeline corridor is entirely domestic. Two independent sources agree.

Owner1=Aramco 100% supported. The Master Gas System and its Phase 3 expansion are wholly owned and operated by Saudi Aramco; SPA is the official Aramco announcement, OGJ reports Aramco awarding the EPC, Blackridge lists Aramco as owner/developer. Sinopec/L&T/Kalpataru are EPC contractors, not owners. Three independent origins agree.
